title: Graphical representation of a reversible first-order reaction R ⇌ P with kb = 4kf
summary: A glass vessel of pure R. Start the reaction and watch R turn into P and P turn back, molecule by molecule, while two rate meters show why it slows: kf[R] falls as R is used up and kb[P] rises as P builds up. The clock stops to make you predict where it will settle, the chamber reaches dynamic equilibrium at 0.8 and 0.2 with the molecules still swapping, an equation board derives it, and only then do you pick the printed graph that matches your own experiment.
subject: Chemistry
subtopics: Rate law for opposing elementary first-order steps
Dynamic equilibrium: forward rate equals backward rate
Equilibrium constant as a ratio of rate constants, K = kf/kb
Integrated rate law for a reversible first-order reaction
concepts: Both directions are elementary first-order steps, so the forward rate is kf[R] and the backward rate is kb[P]; at t = 0 there is no P and the backward rate is exactly zero
Equilibrium is the moment the two rates become equal, kf[R]eq = kb[P]eq - not the moment either reaction stops. Both keep running, molecule by molecule, and only the amounts stop changing
With kb = 4kf, balancing the rates needs four times as much R as P, so [R]eq = 4[P]eq
Every R lost becomes a P, so [R] + [P] = [R]0 at every instant; with [R]eq = 4[P]eq this gives 5[P]eq = [R]0, so [P]eq/[R]0 = 0.2 and [R]eq/[R]0 = 0.8
The equilibrium constant is the ratio of the rate constants: K = [P]eq/[R]eq = kf/kb = 1/4
The plateau depends only on kb/kf; [R]0 cancels in the ratios and the absolute size of kf sets only the time scale
The approach to equilibrium is exponential with the observed constant kf + kb = 5kf, faster than kf alone, because both directions pull towards the balance point

A correct graph must start at 1 and 0, keep [R] + [P] = [R]0, bend over (a first-order approach is always concave down) and level off where the rates balance - option D fails all three of the last tests, option A levels off at kb = kf, option B at kf = 4kb
formulas: [R]/[R]0 = kb/(kf + kb) + kf/(kf + kb) x e^-(kf+kb)t
At equilibrium: kf[R]eq = kb[P]eq,  K = kf/kb

derivedQuantities.option_D: no plateau; P bends upward; R + P falls to about 0.66

methods: Solved independently from the rate law before any key was consulted: d[P]/dt = kf([R]0 - [P]) - kb[P] with [P](0) = 0, equilibrium from kf[R]eq = kb[P]eq and the mass balance
Symbolic: sympy's dsolve of the rate law returns exactly kf[R]0/(kf+kb)(1 - e^-(kf+kb)t); with kb = 4kf it is 0.2(1 - e^-5kf t) with limit 1/5, and [P] is concave down for all t > 0
Numerical: a hand-written RK4 integrator using no closed form agrees with that expression to 3.7e-15 at seven times, keeps [R] + [P] = [R]0 to 2e-15, and plateaus at 0.800000 / 0.200000
Exact rational arithmetic: kf/(kf+kb) = 1/5, kf x 4/5 = kb x 1/5 so detailed balance holds exactly, and K = [P]eq/[R]eq = 1/4 = kf/kb

Stochastic: a Gillespie simulation of 5000 individual molecules settles at P/R0 = 0.196, within the expected fluctuation of 0.2, and keeps converting in both directions after settling (23,699 events after t = 3)

Distractor audit read off the redrawn graphs: (A) plateaus at 0.5/0.5 so K = 1; (B) at R 0.2, P 0.8 so K = 4, the rate constants swapped; (D) has no plateau, its [P] curve is concave up and R + P falls to about 0.66 where the curves cross. Only (C) implies K = 1/4

Robustness: the plateau is independent of [R]0 (2.5 M gives [P]eq = 0.5 M, still 0.2 of [R]0) and of the absolute rate constants (kf = 0.37, kb = 1.48 gives 0.2); explore values kb/kf = 1, 2, 4, 9 give 1/2, 1/3, 1/5, 1/10 exactly
Independent numeric script tests/verify_p1q02.py: 34 of 34 checks pass and the answer is (C)

The page selects the answer letter at run time by comparing the rate law's plateau for the stem's kb/kf with each printed graph's plateau, mass balance and curvature - no letter is written into the page

Headless-browser suite tests/sim_p1q02.js drives the finished page: optional inputs with empty, invalid, negative and fractional entries, the prediction gate holding the clock, molecule counts tracking the rate law within two molecules, the equilibrium event, the counters still climbing at equilibrium, the derivation board, every wrong graph's feedback, the overlay and ticks, the reveal with its blink that stops, replay, reset, explore mode at four ratios and at kb = 0, pause and speed, classroom mode with NEXT held at both gates and PREVIOUS rewinding the chamber, reduced motion, 390 px and 360 px with no overflow, and the real app shell discovering and opening it from the feed with the banner hidden

Answer cross-checked afterwards against the official final key printed with the Paper 1 PDF (Answer Q2: C) and against a published worked solution (ExamSIDE), which gives (C) with [R]/[R]0 decreasing from 1 to 0.8 and [P]/[R]0 increasing from 0 to 0.2
verification.note: Paper 1 of 2026 numbers its questions 1-16 per subject; the combined number of this question is Q.34 (16 Mathematics + 16 Physics + 2). The four option graphs are redrawn as live vector drawings from the paper - dashed [R]/[R]0 and solid [P]/[R]0 as printed - so the exam PDF itself is never published. The stem gives no values for kf or [R]0; the defaults kf = 1 s^-1 and [R]0 = 1 M are convenient starting numbers and the answer does not depend on them.

interactivity: A glass beaker drawn in perspective inside an always-dark chamber, holding 100 molecules - R as blue spheres, P as orange diamonds - that move in three dimensions and flash when they convert; the solution's tint shifts with the composition

The molecule population is slaved to the rate law: each frame the model says how many R -> P and P -> R conversions are due, those molecules flip, and the count stays within one or two molecules of 100[P]/[R]0

Every input is optional and pre-filled with the question's values; START works with every box empty, any empty or invalid box falls back to the question value with a friendly inline note, and a status chip reads USING QUESTION VALUES or USING CUSTOM VALUES
Three inputs - [R]0, kf and kb - each with a typed box that understands fractions, a slider, large - and + steppers and a per-field reset, plus RESET TO QUESTION VALUES and a live kb/kf readout
Two glass rate meters, forward kf[R] and backward kb[P], that visibly converge and glow FORWARD RATE = BACKWARD RATE at equilibrium
A 100 per cent stacked bar showing where the material is, always summing to 1, and two conversion counters that keep climbing at equilibrium

A large live graph of [R]/[R]0 (dashed, as printed) and [P]/[R]0 (solid) drawn from the integrated rate law as the reaction runs, with direct labels, a crosshair tooltip, the equilibrium levels marked once they are reached, the previous run as a grey comparison, and the same numbers as a table
A prediction gate at the moment P -> R wakes up: the clock holds until the student commits to where [P]/[R]0 and [R]/[R]0 will settle, and the chamber checks the prediction when it gets there
A DYNAMIC EQUILIBRIUM REACHED event that leaves the molecules moving and converting
An animated equation board that derives the plateau line by line on the student's own kb/kf and checks it against the molecules in the vessel
A graph challenge with the four printed graphs redrawn and clickable, CHECK ANSWER, a concept-specific explanation for each wrong choice and TRY AGAIN
The chamber's own curve drawn over graph (C), with MOLECULAR SIMULATION, MATHEMATICAL MODEL and GRAPH C ticking in turn
A reveal that dims the laboratory, then sprays OPTION (C) across it with confetti and glowing glyphs, blinks the header answer once and unlocks the solution
EXPLORE MODE with kb/kf = 1, 2, 4 and 9 buttons or any typed values, every change restarting from pure R with the last run kept as a ghost, and kb = 0 showing the irreversible limit
An advanced kinetics panel, collapsed by default, with kobs = kf + kb, tau, the half-way time and a straight-line plot of ln([P]eq - [P]) against time
A four-test table applied to each printed graph, an observation notebook written only when things happen, a trial log with an insight card, and six live mistake cards

CLASSROOM MODE for a projector: the rail and other sections hide, the chamber and graph sit side by side at large size, and NEXT STEP / PREVIOUS STEP walk the teacher through the stages, held at the prediction and at the graph challenge
Pause, 0.5x / 1x / 2x speed, replay, full screen and a theme toggle; reduced-motion users get the full content without the animations
